summary: Installed a daily 02:15 cron job on node1 that runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and appends output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Along the way, fixed the pre-existing script file, which contained leftover heredoc/install artifacts instead of a clean executable script (it was not executable and had garbage trailing lines). Rewrote it as a valid #!/bin/sh script, set 0755 root:root ownership/permissions, and verified it runs successfully. Created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with the schedule "15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1" and confirmed crond is active/enabled. Manually exercised the exact cron command line to confirm it creates and appends to the log file correctly. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and service/data state, issued a safe `shutdown -r now`, polled until the node was reachable again, confirmed the boot_id changed (fb2aa416... -> 160e0496...) proving an actual restart (not just a service bounce), and verified post-restart that crond is active/enabled, the cron.d file and script are intact, the script still runs successfully, and the log file's pre-reboot entry persisted.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS, cron availability (cronie/crond), and the pre-existing /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance script
Found the script file contained broken heredoc/install leftover content and was not executable; rewrote it as a correct #!/bin/sh script and set chown root:root / chmod 0755
Manually ran the script to confirm correct output
Created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with schedule '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and set 0644 perms
Confirmed crond active/enabled and manually executed the exact cron command to verify /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log is created and appended correctly
Captured baseline boot_id, uptime, crond status, cron file, script, and log contents on node1
Triggered a safe reboot (shutdown -r now) backgrounded so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed after reboot, proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: crond active/enabled, cron.d file intact, script executable and functional, and pre-reboot log entry persisted

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled daily at 02:15 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance and retain output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Created /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and verified running that exact command creates/appends the log file with expected content.

evidence.requirement: Script itself is valid, executable, and produces correct output (fixed from a broken pre-existing state)
evidence.summary: Original file had leftover heredoc/install artifacts and no execute bit; rewritten as clean #!/bin/sh script, chmod 0755 root:root, and confirmed correct output on manual run.

evidence.requirement: crond service running to execute the scheduled job
evidence.summary: systemctl is-active/is-enabled crond both report active/enabled before restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart (boot identity, cron config, service, data)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, uptime since 08:09:29, crond active, cron.d file content, script permissions, and existing log content.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned 'reboot triggered' immediately, then subsequent exec calls timed out confirming the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed, proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Two poll attempts timed out while node1 was rebooting; a later poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id 160e0496-f4c2-4565-bcb2-5bb5ca7e3773, different from the pre-restart baseline.

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of cron config, service, script, and data
evidence.summary: After restart: crond active/enabled, /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance intact with correct schedule, script executable and runs correctly, and the pre-reboot log entry (12:10:02Z) persisted in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log.
